study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Tong et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual deviations from normative electroencephalographic connectivity predict antidepressant response

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To develop a normative modeling framework using resting-state EEG (rsEEG) functional connectivity (FC) to quantify individual deviations in patients with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and to use these deviations to predict antidepressant treatment response to sertraline and placebo.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly lists the three cohorts used for the healthy control group.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Overall, we included healthy controls from three independent cohorts and MDD patients from one clinical cohort with antidepressant treatment response data. We integrated three cohorts of 154 healthy controls to ensure our healthy norms represent inter-cohort variability and improve the generalizability of our findings.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Reconstruction error from an autoencoder (original EEG FC matrix - reconstructed EEG FC matrix).
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper defines the deviation metric as the reconstruction error from their autoencoder-based normative model.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: Finally, the difference between the original EEG FC and the reconstructed one, termed reconstruction error, was utilized as the quantification of individual deviation from the healthy norm.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) to select features significantly correlated (Pearson's correlation, p<0.05) with treatment outcome (change in HAMD17 score). LASSO regression was then used to build the final predictive model. Performance was evaluated with Pearson's correlation between predicted and actual outcomes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Individual deviations from a normative model of EEG functional connectivity, derived using an autoencoder, can predict response to both sertraline and placebo in patients with major depressive disorder, outperforming models based on raw connectivity or clinical measures.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The autoencoder-based normative model successfully predicted treatment outcomes for sertraline (r = 0.43, p < 0.001) and placebo (r = 0.33, p < 0.001), outperforming raw EEG FC, PCA-based, and regression-based normative models. Sertraline response was best predicted by deviations in the eyes-open-gamma condition, while placebo response was best predicted by the eyes-closed-beta condition. The predictive models were specific to the treatment arm. Analysis of feature weights suggested sertraline response relies more on transmodal network connectivity, while placebo response relies more on non-transmodal networks.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Findings need replication in additional independent cohorts; the study did not collect post-treatment neuroimaging data to confirm brain connectivity alterations.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Although our results were preliminarily verified with aforementioned analyses, replication studies with additional independent cohorts are important to confirm our findings... as the original protocol of EMBARC study (Trivedi et al., 2016) did not collect neuroimaging data at the end of treatment, we were unable to confirm the brain connectivity alterations mediated by the medications.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study demonstrated that the autoencoder-based individual deviations could distinguish between subclinical (e.g., history of physical/sexual abuse) and diagnostic (e.g., depression severity scores) sources of variability by showing that subclinical measures correlated more with the reconstructed (normative) part of the signal, while diagnostic measures correlated more with the deviation (error) part.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study developed and compared three different normative modeling strategies: PCA-based, regression-based, and autoencoder-based. The autoencoder-based approach, which was the primary method, demonstrated superior performance in predicting treatment response. The study also highlights the specificity of the predictive models, with the sertraline model not predicting placebo response and vice-versa, suggesting distinct neurobiological pathways.
